rows.title: E1: isolate independent executor steps
rows.problem: The executor appended the first result from a previous step even when comparison branches were independent.
rows.change: Dependency-aware context propagation replaced unconditional result concatenation.
rows.verification: F1 rose to 0.349 and average Hop Recall to 0.525 on the 20-question run.
rows.conclusion: Context is useful only when an explicit dependency exists.

rows.title: E2: force Hybrid RRF for document retrieval
rows.problem: Planner-selected retrieval tools produced uneven recall across Chinese, English, and mixed-language reports.
rows.change: Document retrieval steps were routed through keyword and semantic branches with RRF and reranking.
rows.verification: Average Hop Recall increased to 0.650 while system errors remained zero.
rows.conclusion: Retrieval policy materially affected evidence coverage before answer generation.

rows.title: E5: first structured calculation attempt regressed
rows.problem: Free-form extraction mixed company, metric, period, value, and unit scopes.
rows.change: The failure was decomposed into slot extraction, grounding, and deterministic calculation contracts.
rows.verification: The initial E5 result was preserved as failure evidence rather than relabeled as a pass.
rows.conclusion: Deterministic arithmetic is only reliable after fact selection is reliable.

rows.title: E5.1B: machine-readable financial facts
rows.problem: Table parsing and LLM extraction could not consistently preserve financial scope and units.
rows.change: Machine-readable facts and serialized table evidence were introduced behind validated slots.
rows.verification: The original six-document index produced the stronger E5.1B result and was frozen.
rows.conclusion: Structured facts are an Executor tool, not a replacement for Agentic retrieval.

rows.title: Structured Query Stable v1.0
rows.problem: A stable claim required an independent structured test after regression fixes.
rows.change: Structured Test v3 covered direct, entity-dependent, and clarification routes.
rows.verification: 24 fresh samples completed with zero system errors and every structured release gate at 1.0.
rows.conclusion: Structured lookup and multi-fact calculation were frozen as Stable within the declared BT3Y scope.

rows.title: ISSUE-001: unsupported metric escaped the fast path
rows.problem: A carrying-amount question outside Machine Facts returned a wrong value instead of falling back safely.
rows.change: The case became a permanent Safety/Fallback red-test and evidence for non-structured routing work.
rows.verification: The failure, expected answer, trace, and remediation boundary were retained in the engineering record.
rows.conclusion: A stable fast path does not imply stable fallback behavior outside its schema.

rows.title: Dynamic Hop 2 synthesis failed
rows.problem: Semantic similarity did not guarantee logical composability, and runtime-generated partner QA had weaker quality controls.
rows.change: The synthesis design moved from dynamic Chunk-to-QA expansion to Seed-to-Seed candidates with Human Gate.
rows.verification: Low yield and necessary-hop failures were frozen instead of hidden by looser thresholds.
rows.conclusion: Relation validity is not the same as graph eligibility or necessary-hop quality.

rows.title: Necessary-hop and multi-positive evidence recovery
rows.problem: Pairwise Judge decisions could not independently guarantee graph-level edge quality.
rows.change: A bounded recovery used explicit bridge constraints, deduplication, deterministic merge, and human evidence audit.
rows.verification: The candidate-to-edge-to-merge-to-Gold contract closed without reopening unlimited Judge tuning.
rows.conclusion: Human-gated data construction was accepted as an explicit engineering boundary.

rows.title: Textual 2-hop Baseline v0.1
rows.problem: The full-corpus textual system needed an end-to-end result with honest capability boundaries.
rows.change: Development24 ran with Hybrid RRF, reranking, Verifier/Replanner, and Machine Facts disabled for textual questions.
rows.verification: EM 0.250, F1 0.375, Hop Recall 0.479, Full Gold Chain 0.125, and zero system errors were frozen.
rows.conclusion: The pipeline is reproducible, but textual two-hop quality remains Development with known limitations.

rows.title: Qwen3-4B vs Qwen3-8B ablation
rows.problem: The 4B baseline could not separate system limitations from model-capacity limitations.
rows.change: The same Development24 and Agent configuration were rerun with Qwen3-8B and controlled output budgets.
rows.verification: 8B raised Hop Recall from 0.479 to 0.688 and Full Gold Chain from 0.125 to 0.500, while increasing latency and tool use.
rows.conclusion: Model scale matters, but it does not replace retrieval and verifier optimization.
